title: Building an Apprenticeship Strategy for Your Board
description: For leaders deciding how far into apprenticeship to go: referrer, navigator, intermediary, or sponsor. Covers TEGL 05-25 waiver opportunities, the 10 percent co-enrollment goal, navigator staffing models, the pending federal reauthorization, and California's apprenticeship funding streams.
notes: Audience: Executive directors, board members, program directors. Format: HD or executive briefing. Hours assumed from format (HD = 4 hours).
learning_objectives: Assess their board's current apprenticeship capacity and outcomes.
Choose a role (referrer, navigator, intermediary, or sponsor) that fits their resources.
Set a co-enrollment goal and the staffing and training needed to meet it.
Identify the state and federal funding that can pay for the strategy.
prerequisites: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals) or equivalent executive familiarity

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Assessing Your Board's Apprenticeship Capacity; Referrer, Navigator, Intermediary, or Sponsor; Setting a Co-Enrollment Goal and Staffing to It; Funding the Strategy. The closing project ("Project: One-Page Apprenticeship Strategy") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a one-page board apprenticeship strategy with a capacity assessment, chosen role, co-enrollment goal, staffing plan, and funding sources) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (HD or executive briefing; HD = 4 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Prerequisites reflect track order: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals) or equivalent executive familiarity.
